hypothesis: The heat stability of DNA polymerase from thermophilic bacteria increases the efficiency of primer extension at elevated temperatures compared to mesophilic polymerase
prediction: The extension rate of heat-stable DNA polymerase at 95°C will be at least 2.5 times higher than that of a non-heat-stable polymerase at the same temperature
measurement_method: Compare primer extension rates between heat-stable and non-heat-stable DNA polymerases at 95°C using identical primers and DNA templates, measuring the amount of extended product per unit time
falsification_condition: If the extension rate of heat-stable polymerase is less than 1.25 times that of non-heat-stable polymerase at 95°C
